messages.subject: Rattle and PMML
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I recently came accross rattle ... after a few problems with the
installation process, I was able to run it in my pc without problems.
I even was able to export a PMML file from a tree model. I was
wondering though if and when regression models will also be part of
the export ... SVMs?

Thanks,

Alex

Received Fri 11 Jan 2008 10:54am +1100 from Alex:

>

> I recently came accross rattle ... after a few problems with the

> wondering though if and when regression models will also be part of

>

Hi Alex,

Let me know what problems you had in installing, if you get a chance,
as others might have the same problems and it would be useful to
highlight them in the instructions.

Regarding the PMML, no export of SVMs is available yet - it needs
someone to write the code.

There is basic PMML generation from regression models though provided
by the PMML package (part of Rattle). I've not yet added it into the
Rattle interface - will do that soon. For now, after building a regression
model in Rattle, go to the R Console and enter these commands:

> library(pmml)
Loading required package: XML

> pmml.lm(crs$glm)
<PMML version="3.1" xmlns="http://www.dmg.org/PMML-3_1"
xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">
 <Header copyright="Copyright (c) 2007 rg...@indiana.edu"
 description="Linear Regression Model">
  <Extension description="timestamp">2008-01-14 20:40:21</Extension>

...

  </RegressionTable>
 </RegressionModel>
</PMML>

You could save the output from pmml.lm to a file or even cut and paste
to a file.

See the documentation using:

> ?pmml.lm

Hope that helps.

Regards,
Graham

pmml.lm, and so the Export of a Regression model is now in the latest
version of rattle (2.2.83).

Contributions of other PMML generating code is most welcome!

Regards,
Graham

messages.body_plain:
Hi Graham,

Thanks for adding linear regression to rattle. After posting the
message we did find out how to do it from R directly. In any case,
thanks for your help.

As for problems installing rattle. I kept having problems with some
kind of dll file that is part of RGtk2. By looking at other
discussions you had in the group earlier, I found a message in which
you say:

**************************
This looks like you don't have the Gtk library installed on your
system? (It is independent of R and rattle.)

You seem to be using MS/Windows. So could you let me know if you have
installed glade for windows from

        http://gladewin32.sourceforge.net/modules/news/

You need to download gtk-dev-2.10.11-win32-1.exe and then run this
self installing archive.

The install instructions for Rattle are at

        http://datamining.togaware.com/survivor/Installation_Details.html

************************

So, just for the kicks, I installed Glade and then followed the
install instructions for rattle that are described in the link above.
BTW, I could not find a direct link to this link in the togaware
webpage. Maybe you could add it there. It is very helpful.

I don't really remember the sequence of events, but I did need to quit
R after installing different packages. It seems that it helped quite a
bit.

Thanks for your reply,

Alex

Hi Ed,

Sure. You can view any of the source code in R itself either directly
for exported functions (like when you type "rattle") and indirectly
for internal functions (like "rattle:::executeEvaluateScore"). All
source code is also available at
http://code.google.com/p/rattle/source.

A quick way to do what you want is to grab all the source code, put it
into a directory (e.g., "/home/fred/rattle/"), and source all of the files
into R with:

> loc <- "/home/fred/rattle/"
> lapply(paste(loc, grep(".*\\.R$", dir(loc), value=TRUE), sep=""), source)

Then edit whichever files you want, and rerun the lapply command (to
reload your new code).

Also, send me any changes you make as they will probably be useful to
incorporate directly into Rattle for others to use also.

For the "save the observed values with the predicted values when doing
a gaussian glm" I would think a button in the Model tab called Save
Predicted might be useful, with similar functionality to the "Score"
radio button on the Evaluate tab, and modelled on the function
executeEvaluateScore (in rattle.R).

For the  "goodness of fit analysis" I'd add that into the Evaluate
tab.

In both cases, its easy for me to update the GUI if I have sample R
code that implements the functionality you want underneath.

Regards,
Graham

OK, Here is some code I can pass along that allows the Correlation
Cluster Dendrogram to handle much longer variable names by modifying
the right margin.  It also makes the font smaller when there are many
variables.  It probably could use more testing but seems to work fine
for me.

File: rattle.R  (function: executeExploreHiercor)
## Construct the commands.

  cor.cmd    <- sprintf('cc <- cor(%s, use="pairwise")', dataset)
  hclust.cmd <- 'hc <- hclust(dist(cc), "ave")'
  dend.cmd   <- "dn <- as.dendrogram(hc)"

  #Modification by Ed Cox to increase margin for long variable names.
  fontsize <- .75
  if (ncols>45) {fontsize <- .60}
  labwidth <-
eval(parse(text=sprintf('max(as.vector(lapply(colnames(%s),"nchar"),mode="integer"))
+2', dataset)))
  plot.cmd   <- paste('op <- par(mar = c(3,4,3,',labwidth/3.5,'))\n',
                      'plot(dn, horiz=TRUE, ',
                      'nodePar=list(col=3:2, cex=c(2.0, 0.75), pch=
21:22, ',
                      'bg= c("light blue", "pink"), ',
                      'lab.cex = ',fontsize,', lab.col = "tomato"), ',
                      'edgePar=list(col="gray", lwd=2)',
                      ')\n',
                      genPlotTitleCmd("Variable Correlation Clusters",
                                     crs$dataname),'\n',
                      'par(op)\n',
                      sep="")

  ## Start logging and executing the R code.
